# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).

- [Never Hard-Wrap Prose](feedback_never_hard_wrap_prose.md) — PR descriptions and all Markdown: one line per paragraph, never manual line breaks.
- [Succinct Written Artifacts](feedback_succinct_written_artifacts.md) — Changesets, PR bodies, docs: short, plain, no AI slop or backstory.
- [No Session Links](feedback_no_session_links.md) — Never put claude.ai session URLs/Claude-Session trailers in commits or PRs; public repo, private sessions.

- [Budget: Lean Pipeline](feedback_budget_lean_pipeline.md) — weekly token budget; leanest pipeline that still catches bugs; no cleanup agents or rework the user has to review.
- [Use gh stack](feedback_use_gh_stack.md) — stacked PRs must be native GitHub stacks (gh stack link); plain chained PRs get no CI.
- [Agent Context Briefs](feedback_agent_context_briefs.md) — curated 2-4k token briefs, one agent per PR via SendMessage, small fixes directly; no forks of long sessions.

Adversarial read-only review of 17717fc89. I did not run cargo or any tests. Everything below is from reading code and the vendored dependency sources in ~/.cargo/registry (toml_edit 0.22.27, ignore 0.4.33, yaml-rust2). `../callisto-findings/FINDINGS.md` is absent, so nothing was deduplicated against a ledger.

I found no HIGH defect: no common, valid layout in your priority list newly fails. The real findings are medium and low, listed below. Item 1 is the one to fix.

## Findings

### 1. MEDIUM, CONFIRMED (spec drift): `docs/specs/workspace.json` still contradicts the new behavior
- WS-DISC-10 (line ~86) still says "An invalid glob in `members`, `exclude`, `workspaces` or `packages` is ignored while the list's valid entries still apply." The code and WS-DISC-09 now make that an E311 error. This criterion is also tagged `is_error_case`.
- WS-DISC-07 (line 73) says pnpm-workspace.yaml is used "when that file is absent or unusable" and otherwise falls back to package.json `workspaces`. An unparseable or unreadable pnpm file is now an error. The test `read_npm_membership_rejects_a_malformed_pnpm_yaml_even_when_package_json_has_workspaces` asserts the error.
- WS-DISC-12 overclaims. `root.rs::is_workspace_root` only checks that `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `pyproject.toml` exist. It never reads or parses them. Only Cargo.toml and package.json are read or parsed.

### 2. MEDIUM, PLAUSIBLE: the E312 escape hatch ("ignore it in .gitignore") does not work when the workspace root is below the Git toplevel
- Location: `ignore_walk.rs:45-49` (`WalkBuilder` with `.parents(false)` and `.git_ignore(true)`), `mod.rs:77-80` (help text).
- The `ignore` crate applies `.gitignore` rules only if a directory in its parent chain contains `.git` (`dir.rs` `any_git`, `has_git`). With `parents(false)`, that chain is just the walk root.
- Failing input: the Git toplevel is `repo/` and the workspace root is `repo/js/` (found via `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `.moon`). The walk root has no `.git`, so no `.gitignore` is honored. A gitignored symlinked directory that contains a manifest is then walked and fails with E312, and the help text points at a fix that does nothing. The tests miss this because the tempdirs have no `.git`.
- Before this commit that gap only over-discovered. It is now a hard error. Possible fix: `.require_git(false)`, which also changes which paths are skipped.
- No test covers the "link ignored via .gitignore skips it" promise in either layout.

### 3. LOW-MEDIUM, CONFIRMED (silent admit-all remains): pnpm-workspace.yaml whose top level is not a mapping
- Location: `membership.rs:494-500`, `read_pnpm_packages`.
- Failing input: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` containing a bare list such as `- packages/*`, or a scalar.
- `doc["packages"]` on a non-Hash yields BadValue, so the function returns `Ok(None)` and the whole repo is admitted. This is the failure mode the commit set out to close, and a bare list is a plausible user mistake. It should be an E311 error.
- Only documents after the first are ignored, which matches pnpm.
- The same shape-blindness applies to a root `package.json` whose top level is not an object, such as `[]`. It yields no `workspaces` and no `name`, so admit-all (`membership.rs:462,471`).

### 4. LOW, CONFIRMED (tests that would pass with the production change reverted)
- `toml_edit` 0.22 already skips a leading BOM (`parser/document.rs:36-37`). Because of that, these TOML BOM tests are vacuous:
  - `read_cargo_membership_reads_a_manifest_that_starts_with_a_byte_order_mark`
  - root.rs `a_workspace_root_manifest_with_a_byte_order_mark_is_still_a_workspace_root`
  - cargo_tests.rs `open_context_reads_a_root_manifest_that_starts_with_a_byte_order_mark`, which also asserts only `is_some()`
- The `strip_prefix` added in `cargo.rs:709-712` is redundant.
- A side effect: `WorkspaceCargoResolver::persist` writes `document.to_string()` with no BOM, so a version bump to a BOM'd root Cargo.toml drops the BOM. package.json and `pre.json` preserve it.
- The BOM tests with real signal are the package.json one, which previously fell back to admit-all, and the pnpm path via `read_root_manifest`.
- These tests are fine but also pass before the change, since they cover valid behavior that did not change:
  - `a_symlink_that_holds_no_package_is_ignored`
  - the "absent table admits all" tests
  - `a_pnpm_workspace_yaml_without_a_packages_key_admits_everything`
  - `open_context_for_a_root_with_no_manifests_is_empty`
- Missing coverage:
  - No test for a symlink to an in-repo directory.
  - No test for a symlinked platform candidate (`ignore_walk.rs:179-181`).
  - No test for an npm `workspaces` object without `packages` (it errors) or for `workspaces: null` (also errors).
  - No test for an inline or dotted Cargo `[workspace]` table, or for a uv `[tool.uv.workspace]` that is malformed in shape. Python is tested only for unparseable TOML.
  - No test for CRLF or YAML-anchor pnpm files.

### 5. LOW, CONFIRMED: stale comment and changeset
- `ignore_walk.rs:50-53` still says symlinked package directories "are a supported workspace pattern -- discovery follows them deliberately". That is now the opposite of the behavior, and the comment is also multi-line prose.
- `.changeset/loud-owls-refuse.md` bundles three topics: fail-closed membership, symlink rejection, and BOM and Yarn-classic acceptance. AGENTS.md asks for one changeset per user-visible topic. It also never mentions that Yarn classic `{ "packages": [...] }` is now read, which is user-visible.

### 6. LOW, CONFIRMED (pre-existing, not a regression): membership globs for `./x` and `x/` forms
- `build_globset` (`membership.rs:82`) does not normalize leading `./` or trailing `/`.
- `"workspaces": ["./packages/*"]` or `"packages/*/"` is accepted by npm, Yarn and Cargo but silently matches nothing here. Those packages are dropped with no error.
- The commit's intent is to stop silent membership drops, so this is worth a follow-up or an explicit note.

### 7. LOW, PLAUSIBLE: strictness that could affect real repos
- `toml_edit` is pinned to 0.22 (TOML 1.0). A root or ancestor Cargo.toml using TOML 1.1 syntax now hard-fails at `root.rs:50-54`, `membership.rs:207` and `cargo.rs` load. Before, it was silently skipped. Members already had this limit.
- `find_workspace_root` now parses every ancestor Cargo.toml and package.json up to the Git toplevel, in both loops. A malformed manifest in a fixture or template directory that sits between cwd and the toplevel now errors, where it was skipped before. That matches the stated policy, but it is a behavior change. A root `Cargo.toml` that is a template with placeholders in a non-Rust repo now breaks every command.

## Swallowed read or parse errors still in the touched files
- `ignore_walk.rs:24`: `dunce::canonicalize(root).unwrap_or_else(..)`.
- `ignore_walk.rs:74`: `path.is_dir()` turns a metadata error into "skip".
- `root.rs:16`: `canonicalize(start)` fallback.
- `root.rs:96`: `.moon` `.is_dir()` swallows permission errors.
- `ignore_walk.rs:150`: `eprintln!` warning for a bad manifest in a directory that no membership explicitly admits (the documented behavior). With no `members` restriction, a malformed child manifest is only a warning and the package is dropped.
- `ignore_walk.rs:170`: `PackageId::parse(..).unwrap_or_else(Bare)`.
- `walk.rs:274,289,754,833`: `.ok()` on manifest open. A package.json that fails to open is silently treated as a Canonical, non-platform role at `walk.rs:289`. Only the `for_workspace_root` call at line 90 was changed in that file.
- Pre-existing asymmetry: `root.rs::has_explicit_table` ignores `workspace = {..}` (inline) and dotted `workspace.members = ..`, while `read_membership` accepts both. A virtual manifest written that way is not recognized as a workspace root, so you get E030 or a different root.

## Checked and fine
- **`for_workspace_root` and `workspace_package_version`:** `inheritance()` can only fail on a `[workspace.package] version` string that is not valid SemVer. A non-string version returns `None`, not an error. Valid Cargo versions parse, so no valid manifest newly errors. Dotted and inline `workspace.package.version` lookups work through `Item::get`.
- **Cargo and uv membership:** negation, `exclude`, a hybrid root, and `members` with no `[workspace]` all behave as before. `[workspace.package]` or `[workspace.dependencies]` only gives `members: None`, so everything is admitted. A uv root pyproject with neither table gives `cursor: None`, so unrestricted. Inline and dotted tables parse through `Item::get` and `as_table_like`.
- **npm:**
  - Array `workspaces`, the yarn-classic object with `packages`, a private root with an array, empty `workspaces` (admits none, hybrid root kept) and `name`-based hybrid detection all behave correctly.
  - The only failing shape is an object without `packages`. Yarn requires `packages`, so this is acceptable.
- **pnpm:** `catalog:`, `overrides:`, anchors, CRLF, multiple documents (first only), a missing or null `packages` key, negation and `packages: []` are all fine. BOM is stripped. Utf-8 errors map to E310.
- **Variants in the table-driven test:** `malformed_workspace_membership_is_an_error` asserts the right variant per row. Parse maps to `ManifestParseError`, shape or glob to `InvalidMembership`, and the file name is checked. It does not assert error codes. `LocateError` has no `Read` row there, but read errors are covered in unit tests.
- **Deleted tests:** the deleted "falls back" tests are replaced by error-asserting ones. Valid-behavior coverage (negation, hybrid root, empty arrays, exclude-only, pnpm precedence) is kept.
- **Symlink check:**
  - `reject_symlinked_package` checks every component of `rel`, including the final one. A symlink above the root is not in `rel`, and the root is canonicalized, so macOS `/var` is not a false positive. `Path::new(".")` yields `CurDir`, and `lstat(root/.)` is a directory.
  - `node_modules` and the other skip names are filtered by `filter_entry` before descent, so pnpm links are safe. Hidden directories (`.venv`, `.yarn`, `.next`) are skipped.
  - A gitignored symlink is skipped by the walker, provided `.gitignore` is honored (see finding 2).
  - A non-admitted symlinked package is ignored, which matches the spec.
  - An in-repo link to another in-repo package directory is rejected only if the link path is admitted (the real path is yielded separately). That is policy-consistent.
- **Other locators:** `IgnoreWalkLocator` is the only `ProjectLocator` impl, so no other locator bypasses the check. `platform_owners` and the path-dependency resolution in `walk.rs` only consume paths already produced by the locator.
- **Code citing specs:** no spec IDs appear in code, tests or messages. The new `mod.rs` messages are fine. E310, E311 and E312 are in `docs/errors.md`. The "240 numeric codes" footer is already stale before this commit.
- **Not checked:** I did not test whether `yaml-rust2` rejects exotic but valid pnpm YAML that pnpm itself accepts. That is newly fatal where it used to fall back.
